source: Mahabharata, Critical Edition (BORI), Adi Parva, Astika sub-parva, adhyaya 16 (vv. 1–15 approx.): Ananta uproots Mandara at Brahma's and Narayana's word; the gods and asuras bring it to the ocean, which asks for a share of the amrita; the king of tortoises Akupara bears the mountain, set on his back by Indra; Vasuki is the rope.
structure: From episode 11: COLD OPEN (the hook over the episode's strongest image, big on-screen text from frame 1; KIT.series.hookCard) → title (the hook's post) → RECAP (≈2.5 s) → STORY (with a brief cut to Sauti at the Naimisha fire) → the cliffhanger image + line → a silent ≈1.5 s Next card that dissolves back into the first frame (KIT.series.loopNextScene).

strings.episodeTitle: A Mountain for a Churning Stick

voice.note: speaker → script/cast.json (voice, speed, pitch). Per line: speed (× the speaker's), pre/post (ms of silence before/after the voice), say (what is spoken, if not `text`). captionY (px or "high") lifts the caption above low action.

lines.speaker: sauti
lines.text: Who could tear a mountain from the earth?
lines.say: Who could tear a mountain from the earth?
lines.note: COLD OPEN (moving from frame 1): a forested mountain heaving up out of the torn earth, roots and rock falling, a white serpent's seven hoods rising behind it; the fire licks up from the bottom edge. The question in big text from frame 1 (caption off). beats = 'tear' (the ground splits), 'mountain'. The title in the post.

lines.text: Narayana told the gods and asuras: churn the ocean together.
lines.say: Narayana told the gods and asuras: [p:80] churn the ocean together.
lines.note: RECAP (short): episode 11's key image as a memory: Narayana in his aureole, Brahma beside him.

lines.speaker: elder_sage
lines.text: But with what could anyone churn an ocean?
lines.say: But with what could anyone churn an ocean?
lines.note: FRAME (the Naimisha fire, from Sauti's side this time): the elder sage Shaunaka leans toward Sauti and asks; Sauti, in the foreground, lifts his hand. beats = 'with what', 'ocean'.

lines.text: With Mandara: a mountain of forests, as deep below the earth as it rose above.
lines.say: With Mandara: [p:100] a mountain of forests, [p:80] as deep below the earth as it rose above.
lines.note: STORY 1. NEW PLACE AND LIGHT: the plain of the world in clear high daylight, Mandara standing in it; the camera tilts down through the cut-away earth to its roots, as deep as it is tall (beats[1] 'below'), and back up ('above'). Name card.

lines.text: At Brahma's word and Narayana's, the serpent Ananta tore it from the ground.
lines.say: At Brahma's word and Narayana's, [p:250] the serpent Ananta tore it from the ground.
lines.note: STORY 2. A 250 ms rest, then the reveal: Ananta, the white serpent of seven hoods, rises, coils round the mountain, and on 'tore' (beats[3], a drum and boom) Mandara rips out of the earth, roots streaming, rock falling. Name card.

lines.text: Gods and asuras carried it to the shore of the sea.
lines.say: Gods and asuras carried it to the shore of the sea.
lines.note: STORY 3. Evening on the shore: the two hosts, side by side for once, carry the mountain high on their raised arms across the frame toward the sea. beats = 'Gods', 'carried', 'sea'.

lines.speaker: samudra
lines.text: Churn me, then. But I too must have my share of the amrita.
lines.say: Churn me, then. [p:150] But I too must have my share of the amrita.
lines.note: STORY 4 · THE TURN (≈ 50 %): a 350 ms rest, then the Ocean himself rises from the waves, a crowned king of the waters, a wave breaking behind him; on 'share' (beats[1]) he lifts a pearl and a branch of coral. A bell on 'Churn'.

lines.text: Akupara, king of the tortoises, took the mountain on his back.
lines.say: Akupara, [p:100] king of the tortoises, took the mountain on his back.
lines.note: STORY 5. Under the surface: a vast ancient tortoise rises from the deep (beats[0], his name card); Indra above, vajra raised, sets the mountain on his shell (beats[2] 'back', a drum).

lines.text: And Vasuki, king of the serpents, was wound round it for a rope.
lines.say: And Vasuki, [p:100] king of the serpents, [p:60] was wound round it for a rope.
lines.note: STORY 6. Vasuki, violet and gold, winds round the mountain turn by turn (the helix grows: beats[1] → beats[2]); name card.

lines.text: The gods took one end, the asuras the other.
lines.say: The gods took one end, [p:100] the asuras the other.
lines.note: STORY 7. The whole rig: gods at the tail on the left, asuras at the head on the right, taking hold (beats[0] gods, beats[1] asuras). The CE does not say who held which end; the picture leaves the head with the asuras, as the tradition shows it, without naming it.

lines.text: They began to churn, and the ocean began to burn.
lines.say: They began to churn… [p:100] and the ocean began to burn.
lines.note: NEXT 1 (cliffhanger image): the mountain begins to turn, the hosts haul; on 'burn' (beats[1]) fire pours from Vasuki's mouths and the forests on the mountain catch fire, red light on the milk-white water.

lines.text: Next: What Rose from the Ocean
lines.note: The short, silent Next card (KIT.series.loopNextScene): a glimpse of episode 13, the Moon rising from the white sea; then the fire rises and the first frame returns (loop).
